elder.summary: Old Bram. The oldest man in Hearthmere. He sits by the well and watches who comes down the road, and says less than he knows.

about.elda: Feeds half the village and scolds the other half. Her boy is with the levy. Don't ask her about him unless you mean to listen.
about.lina: Counts other people's coin and calls it trade. She was not always so. Debt does that.
about.mira: Runs the Guild while Corwin drinks it. She came here at eight years old with nothing. Ask her where from and watch her smile go flat.
about.garrick: A tired man doing two men's work. Tired men look the other way. Remember that.
about.smith: Tess. Her husband went to the salt pits to pay a debt. Three years. She still sets two cups.
about.kai: One of yours. Thinks none of this is real. The day he learns better, somebody else will pay for the lesson.
about.sora: Another of yours, and the only one who reads. She asks me about the old stones. I tell her less than she'd like.
about.wren: Good hands, old fear. She left the Church, and the Church does not like to be left.

barks.text: Three this year. Three.
Well's low. It was never low in my day.
Sit, if you're sitting. Standing makes the ale nervous.

elda.summary: Elda the baker. Up before the sun, feeds anyone who looks thin, and has opinions about all of them. Her son Jory serves in the margravine's levy.

about.elder: Bram was old when I was a girl. He knows every grave in the yard by name. Bring him bread and he pretends he didn't want it.
about.pip: Good boy. Works that farm like it was three of him. His father owes the Company and thinks nobody knows.
about.lina: She sells flour at a price that makes me want to spit in it. But she pays on the day. I'll say that.
about.garrick: He eats here every morning and has not paid since the thaw. I let him. Somebody has to stand at that gate.
about.smith: Tess keeps her fire lit and her mouth shut. I'd take one of her over ten of most people.

barks.text: First loaves are out! Don't all stand there.
You're thin. Everyone who falls here is thin.

smith.summary: Tess, who keeps the forge. Her husband Orrin was bonded to the Saltdeeps three years ago for a debt. She has had no word since.

about.lina: Ask her what a husband costs. She'll have the figure.
about.elda: She leaves a loaf on my anvil when she thinks I'm not eating. I'm not, mostly.
about.elder: He sits. He watches. When my Orrin was taken he was the only one who said it was wrong, out loud, in the square.
about.garrick: He was at the gate the day they took Orrin through it. He opened it.

barks.text: Saltmere. He's at Saltmere.
Iron's dear this year. Ask the goblins where it all goes.

lina.summary: Lina, who trades from the stall by the square. Everything she sells comes through the Halveth Company, and so does everything she owes.

about.smith: Tess blames me for a contract her husband put his own mark to. I only carried the paper.
about.elder: The old man thinks the village ran better before coin. It ran hungrier.
about.garrick: A reasonable man. Reasonable men are worth cultivating.
about.wren: She undersells the Company's tonics and thinks nobody in East Watch has noticed. Somebody has.
about.elda: She would give the bakery away loaf by loaf if nobody stopped her.

barks.text: A reeve who can read a contract. That's all I say.
Company goods, Company prices. Fresh off the East Watch road.

wren.summary: Wren the alchemist, with a stall by the Guild road. She trained under the Church of the Pale Lantern and left without leave.

about.mira: She gave me this pitch when nobody else would rent to a woman with no past. I don't forget it.
about.lina: She has asked twice where I learned my craft. She smiles when she asks.
about.sora: She brings me rubbings from the old stones and asks what the marks do. I tell her the truth: I was never taught that far.
about.elder: He looks at my hands, not my face. He knows whose hands were trained like these.

barks.text: Red for wounds. Don't drink two at once, whatever Kai says.

garrick.summary: Garrick, the village guard. One man for a gate, a road and the nights. He takes what he is offered, and he is offered things.

about.kai: Your kind die and get up again. He acts like it. One night he'll start something in that yard that a village man has to finish.
about.elda: Best bread in the March. I owe her since the thaw. She hasn't asked.
about.lina: Pays her dues, keeps her stall tidy. I don't ask what's in the crates. That isn't my post.
about.smith: She hasn't spoken a civil word to me in three years. She has her reasons.
about.elder: Knows more than he says. Lets you find out the hard way.

barks.text: Boars. I told him boars.
Road's quiet. I like it quiet.
Nights are long at this gate.

pip.summary: Pip of Harrow Farm. Works the fields with his father Hamm, and keeps a pitchfork by the door since the goblins grew bold.

about.elda: She used to give me the burnt ends when I was small. Still does. Don't tell her I said still.
about.garrick: He's one man. One. You count the goblins and tell me that's enough.
about.elder: Da says Old Bram fell out of the sky same as you, and Bram says Da talks too much.

barks.text: I heard her shout. I heard her.
Walk past the sheep, don't run. They bolt.

mira.summary: Mira, receptionist of the Hearthmere Guild, who runs it in all but name. Cheerful with everyone. She came to the village as a child, from the north.

about.hollis: Twenty years with the Company before he came to us. He reads a ledger the way priests read scripture.
about.kai: He brings in more crystals than anyone and more trouble than the rest together.
about.sora: She pays her dues and asks for the keys to the old records. I've stopped asking why.
about.wren: The best alchemist this side of East Watch, and she charges like the worst. Buy from her.
about.elder: Bram found me on the north road when I was eight. He has never once asked me about it.

hollis.summary: Hollis, the Guild's appraiser. Kept the Halveth Company's books in East Watch for twenty years before he came to Hearthmere.

about.mira: She adds faster than I do and pretends she doesn't. Sensible girl.
about.lina: She trades on Holt's paper. I wrote that paper for twenty years. I know what the small script says.
about.kai: Brings me pelts hacked to ribbons and argues the price. Every time.

kai.summary: Kai, a Lightborn who fell a year ago. A fine swordsman who treats the world as a game he is winning.

about.sora: She thinks there's a way home. I tell her this is the better server. She doesn't laugh.
about.garrick: Level nothing, guards a gate. Why do they even give him a name?
about.mira: Best quest-giver in the zone. I mean that as a compliment. She doesn't take it as one.

barks.text: Next round's on whoever died last. Not me, then.

sora.summary: Sora, a Lightborn who fell a year ago. She studies the old Auren stones and believes there is a way back.

about.kai: He stopped counting the days. I think that is how it gets you.
about.wren: She was taught to read part of the old script and forbidden the rest. She helps me anyway.
about.elder: He answers my questions with questions. But they are always the right questions.

nell.summary: Nell of Westwood, bonded to the Halveth Company for her father's debt of fifteen crowns. She was in the cage with you.

corwin.summary: Corwin Hale, Branch Master of the Hearthmere Guild. A-rank once; Greyfang took his leg and the drink took the rest. He sits in the tavern yard and misses nothing.

about.mira: Runs my branch better than I ever did, and lets me keep the title. I'd die for that girl. Easier than filling in her ledgers.
about.edwin: Good heart, good arm, no fear. Two of those will get him killed. I signed his badge myself. I think about that.
about.kai: Fights like the world owes him a second try. It does, for him. Stand behind him, never beside him.
about.elder: Bram remembers things this valley has paid to forget. Buy him a drink and listen. Don't push.
about.garrick: One guard, three roads. I've stopped blaming him for what he doesn't see.
about.hollis: Twenty years a clerk before he came to us. Knows iron and hides, and what both are worth to the wrong people.

barks.text: Too bright. Who ordered morning?
Mira! Is the board full? ...Good girl.
Count them in. Always count them in.

tam.summary: Tam, Hollis's apprentice at the Guild's side counter. Eager, careful, and afraid of the one mistake that costs his master money.

about.hollis: He says 'again' more than he says my name. But he's never once docked me. I looked in the book.
about.mira: She saves me the heel of the loaf. She pretends she doesn't.
about.kai: He let me hold his sword once. It's heavier than it looks. Everything is.

barks.text: Twelve boar hides, nine fair, three poor. Twelve.
Tower is East Watch. Three waves is Saltmere...

edwin.summary: Edwin, leader of the Brightwater Four: four Hearthmere-born adventurers at rank F. Sure of himself, kind, and certain that somebody from here ought to do this work.

about.moss: Sees a rabbit's track on bare stone. Says nine words a day, and eight are about your feet.
about.fen: She's why the rest of us still have all our fingers. Don't tell her she's the brave one. She'll argue.
about.rook: He'd stand in front of a falling tree if you asked him nicely. Sometimes if you didn't.
about.kai: He's what we'd be if dying didn't count. I don't know whether I envy him.
about.corwin: He signed our badges and then didn't speak for an hour. He was A-rank. One day I'll ask him what it's like.

barks.text: Board first, then breakfast. Rook. Board first.
To Brightwater! And to whoever's buying.

moss.summary: Moss, the archer of the Brightwater Four. Quiet, dry, and the first to notice what the ground has to say.

about.edwin: He walks in front. Somebody has to. I'd rather it wasn't always him.
about.rook: Loud. Useful. The goblins look at him, and I get a clean shot.
about.fen: Counts our bandages every night. If the number worries her, we don't go out.

barks.text: Wind's from the south.
...Heel first. Every one of them.

fen.summary: Fen, healer of the Brightwater Four. She patches the other three with herbs bought from Wren on credit, and keeps a list of everything that could go wrong.

about.wren: She taught me which mushrooms mend and which only look as if they do. She never says where she learned it.
about.edwin: He thinks if he's brave enough, nobody gets hurt. It doesn't work like that. I have the needle to prove it.
about.rook: Four stitches this month. He named them.
about.moss: He notices everything, and tells you a day later.

barks.text: Feverleaf, two bundles. And the red, if she'll trust me for it.
Rook. Sleeve. Show me the arm.

rook.summary: Rook, the shield of the Brightwater Four. Loud, hungry and hard to knock over. His brother Dunn weds the miller's daughter.

about.osric: Weighs the flour twice and my brother three times. Dunn's a good man. Osric will work that out by the wedding, or after.
about.anwen: Soon to be my sister. Kind. Quiet. Looks down the east road a lot, for a bride.
about.fen: She sews straight. I've the arm to show for it. Want to see?
about.elda: The finest woman in the March. I'd marry her bread.

barks.text: It BIT me. A slime! Look at it!
Is that bread? I smell bread.
And then it hit the shield. BANG. Like that.

osric.summary: Osric, miller of Mill Hill and a voice on the village council. Tight with coin, proud of his stones, prouder of his daughter Anwen.

about.anwen: My girl. Reads, sews, keeps the tally better than I do. Dunn had better deserve her. I've told him so, twice.
about.elda: Pays on the day, every week, for thirty years. If the rest of the March paid like Elda there'd be no Company.
about.lina: Sharp. Too sharp. She offered me a price for next year's flour before this year's wheat was cut. I said I'd think. I'm still thinking.
about.rook: Eats like two men and pays like half of one. But he'd stand between my girl and a wolf. I've seen worse kin.
about.hamm: Good farmer in a bad year. He signed with the Company. I told him not to. He had children to feed; I had only advice.

barks.text: Wind's fair. Stones are turning. Good.
Twenty-four sacks. I counted twenty-four.

anwen.summary: Anwen, the miller's daughter, to be married on the twenty-fourth. Gentle, nervous, and never once out of the valley.

about.osric: Father counts things so he doesn't have to say them. Forty sacks means he's pleased. He's counted the wedding guests four times.
about.sora: She lends me books. Real ones, from the Guild shelf. She says where she comes from, everyone can read. Imagine.
about.rook: He'll be my brother soon. He's promised not to make a speech. Nobody believes him.
about.maddy: She says she'll leave the day she turns eighteen. She says it every year, about every birthday.

barks.text: Blue thread. No, the grey. ...The blue.
The road looks longer at dusk.

hamm.summary: Hamm Harrow, Pip's father, master of Harrow Farm and a voice on the council. Worn thin by a bad year and a debt to the Halveth Company.

about.pip: My boy. He was never a frightened child. Then one of yours burned the barn. He's twenty and he checks the latch three times a night.
about.maddy: My brother's girl. Mouth like a magpie. Does two men's work and tells you about it.
about.tobias: Twelve years here and maybe a hundred words. I'd trust him with the deed to the land.
about.lina: She brought the Company's paper to my table and called it a kindness. Might be it was. Ask me at harvest.
about.osric: Told me not to sign. He was right. Being right has never yet fed a cow.

barks.text: Two of mine. Out of my own yard.
Far fence is down again.
Rain by week's end, or we carry water.

maddy.summary: Maddy, Pip's cousin, seventeen, who works Harrow Farm and means to see the world past the south gate.

about.pip: Jumps at his own shadow since the barn. He used to climb the mill sails for a dare. I miss that Pip.
about.tobias: Says nothing all day and then one thing at supper that's right. It's very annoying.
about.hamm: Uncle thinks if he works hard enough the debt will get embarrassed and leave.
about.kai: He winked at me once. Pip didn't speak to me for a week. Worth it.

barks.text: Tobias! You owe me a copper!
One day. Straight down that road.

tobias.summary: Tobias, the hired man at Harrow Farm these twelve years. He says little and sees the fences every night.

about.maddy: Talks for both of us. Suits me.
about.garrick: I told him about the fence. He said boars.

barks.text: Hm.

vosk.summary: Brann Vosk, captain of the finders who wait at Mirror Lake for those who fall from the sky.
fight: Cut them down! Don't let them reach the cage!
Gil! The one on the right!

gil.summary: Gil, Vosk's net man: quick, sly and too pleased with himself.
fight: Come on, then, you ugly little rat!

hanne.summary: Hanne, the steadiest of the finders, an old soldier with a short sword.

corb.summary: Corb, the big one with the club, slow to speak and slow to quit.
corb.death: Too many... too many of them...

rhea.summary: Rhea, the Guild's examiner, who teaches every new adventurer to fight before they go out.

barks.text: Mind the chips. They fly.
Forty cords before the frost, and the Guild hall burns twenty of them.
Saw a thornback's tracks by the creek. Walk wide of the jungle, lad.
Good fire. Best part of the day, this.
Uncle says I swing like a goose. Geese don't swing!
One day I'll take a job off the Guild board. Just you watch.
Is that stew? Tell me that's stew.
